note: WHAT THIS IS: the Trae-side SSE bytes our decoder is fed, written down as an explicit specimen so the contract test can compare our parser against the pinned upstream parser byte for byte.

WHAT IT IS NOT: a live capture. Nothing here was recorded from the gateway — we are offline tonight, and no request was made. Event NAMES and payload FIELDS follow the shapes already recorded from observation in 进展.md:55-63 and src/protocol.ts:9-16; the framing (CRLF, chunk splits, multi-line data, id/retry, bare data, [DONE]) is the SSE specification's, not ours.

WHY IT STILL COUNTS: the two things under contract here — the set of `event:` names and the framing rules — are exactly what the upstream parser implements, and they can be compared on constructed bytes just as well as on captured ones. A divergence found here is a real divergence; the file says nothing about whether Trae emits any given event.
`chunks` are the byte boundaries the decoder is fed at: several deliberately split a line, an event name, and a CRLF pair, because that is what a socket does.

canonical.why: One pass over every named event both implementations know, plus an unknown name, an error carrying `extra`, a multi-line data payload, id/retry fields and the [DONE] sentinel.

emitProbe.why: The Trae-side input that drives OUR downstream emission: token_usage, a thinking delta, two text deltas, a tool-call delta, then done. What comes out is written to the pi-ai-facing socket exactly as src/shim.ts:239 and :248 write it — and the reference's own SseDecoder is pointed at those bytes, so 'we emit something it understands' is checked on real output, not on intent.

probes.why: `event: token_usage ` with a trailing space. We trim the name; the reference strips one leading space only.
An SSE comment line, then a blank line with no data before it. Both must ignore the comment and emit nothing for the empty dispatch.

A `data` line with no colon. The SSE specification reads that as the field `data` with an empty value, so an event IS dispatched with an empty payload — this is where we and the reference part company.
The stream's last line IS newline-terminated but no blank line closes the event. Both parsers must still flush the tail, so the answer must not be lost.

The stream ends mid-line, with no trailing newline at all — an aborted connection, or a proxy that closes without the final CRLF. The reference's finish() consumes the leftover buffer before dispatching; this probe exists to find out what we do with it.
`event:` with an empty value. The reference omits the key entirely; we keep an empty string — both must still decode the delta by its payload.
The chunk boundary falls between the CR and the LF of a CRLF pair — the classic socket split.
